title: Restriction respects pointwise equality
statement: Let $f, g : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2\text{-valued Boolean inputs}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be two Boolean functions on $n$ variables that agree everywhere, $f(y) = g(y)$ for every input $y$, and let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables. Then the restricted functions agree as well: writing $f_\rho(x) = f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ for the restriction of $f$ by $\rho$, one has $f_\rho(x) = g_\rho(x)$ for every $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$.
hypotheses_covered: f and g agree pointwise: f(y) = g(y) for all y
rho is a restriction on n variables
replaced:
If two Boolean functions $f$ and $g$ agree at every input, then for any restriction
$\rho$ their restrictions agree pointwise: $\mathrm{restrictFn}\, f\,\rho\,x = \mathrm{restrictFn}\, g\,\rho\,x$
for all $x$.
